title: dinosaur
summary: An ancient animal with a surprisingly modern name. Investigate a scientific report, then decode its Greek ingredients.
question: Where did this word come from?
completion: dinosaur ← Dinosauria, a scientific Latin name published in England in 1842 ← Greek deinos + sauros. The animals are ancient; this scientific name is modern. New names can be built from very old word parts.
partner: A similar sound is a clue. Let’s check the evidence.

evidence.title: A report from 1842

evidence.title: Build a name with Greek
evidence.text: Deinos means terrible or fearfully great; sauros means lizard. Owen combined these ancient Greek ingredients in his modern scientific name. Ancient Greeks did not use Dinosauria for these animals.

puzzles.title: Triceratops
puzzles.text: Three-horned face: two large horns above the eyes and a smaller horn on the nose. Its scientific name uses Greek word parts.

puzzles.title: Stegosaurus
puzzles.text: Roof lizard: the name refers to its plates, which were originally thought to lie flat like a covering. Spot the lizard ingredient again!

puzzles.title: Diplodocus
puzzles.text: Double beam: the name refers to the shape of bones underneath its tail, rather than its long neck. The name uses Greek ingredients.

puzzles.title: T. rex
puzzles.text: T. stands for Tyrannosaurus. Its name mixes Greek ingredients for tyrant and lizard with Latin rex, meaning king.
